user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Detection-to-segmentation pseudo-mask self-distillation
SUMMARY: Use the image-label-trained detection branch's multi-level patch maps, filtered by cross-level agreement, as pseudo-masks to train the segmentation branch with MVFA's existing Dice and Focal losses, iterating twice.
HYPOTHESIS: Two rounds of detection-to-segmentation self-distillation retain at least 75% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance on held-out modalities, and the cross-level agreement filter yields pseudo-masks with at least 1.5x the precision of single-level (deepest layer) pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: source of segmentation supervision (true masks vs. pseudo-masks from the detection branch vs. none). Round 0: train MVFA with the detection loss only (all source images). Pseudo-mask for an abnormal training image: patches whose det-branch anomaly probability is in the top 5% of the image at at least 3 of 4 levels, upsampled and restricted to the foreground; for normal images the pseudo-mask is empty (all-normal). Round 1-2: train segmentation adapters with Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks (pixels outside confident regions in abnormal images are ignored in the Focal term). Dependent variables: pseudo-mask precision/recall against true masks (where available, measurement only), pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: MVFA already trains a detection branch on image labels for every source image, and its multi-level patch maps contain coarse localisation. These maps can be turned into pseudo-masks that supervise the segmentation branch with MVFA's own Dice and Focal losses, so the segmentation adapters learn from image labels indirectly, through a teacher that never saw a mask.
METHOD: 1) train_zero.py: stage A trains det_adapters only (existing else-branch for all images). 2) New script make_pseudo_masks.py: run the det branch on all source training images, compute per-level probability maps (17x17), mark patches in the image-wise top 5% at >= 3 levels, upsample to 240x240 with nearest neighbour, AND with a foreground mask (Otsu); save as PNG next to images. 3) Stage B: train seg_adapters with the existing Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for every image (normal: empty mask), Focal ignoring unlabelled pixels via a weight map. 4) Repeat pseudo-mask generation once from the stage-B seg branch (round 2). 5) Hyper-parameters as MVFA (lr 1e-4, 50 epochs per stage, batch size 1).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); masks of the source datasets are discarded for all image-label-supervised variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities using image AUROC only (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds; evaluation on the held-out modalities that have masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) for pixel metrics and on all six for image AUROC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; det-branch maps used directly as segmentation output (no distillation); single-level pseudo-masks. Ablations: agreement threshold (2, 3, 4 levels); top-percentage (2%, 5%, 10%); number of rounds. Metrics: pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC; pseudo-mask precision/recall on BrainMRI/LiverCT/RESC training images (analysis only). Falsification: retention below 60% or no improvement over using det-branch maps directly.

Idea B:
TITLE: Asymmetric patch-level MIL with a SigLIP loss for mask-free segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Train MVFA's segmentation adapters from image labels only: every patch of a normal image is pushed to the normal anchor and the top-2% patches of an abnormal image to the abnormal anchor, with a sigmoid (SigLIP-style) patch-text loss at all four levels.
HYPOTHESIS: Asymmetric SigLIP-MIL training on image labels from all five source datasets retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's zero-shot pixel-level AUROC margin over chance ((AUROC - 0.5) ratio) on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and outperforms symmetric top-k MIL (same k for both classes) by at least 2 pixel-AUROC points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: segmentation supervision (Dice+Focal on masks vs. asymmetric MIL on image labels). For level l and patch j with cosine similarities to the normal and abnormal anchors, logits z_j = t * (cos(f_j, T_abn) - cos(f_j, T_nor)) + b with learnable temperature t and bias b. Loss for a normal image: mean_j log(1 + exp(z_j)) over all 289 patches. Loss for an abnormal image: mean over the top-k patches (k = 6, 2%) of log(1 + exp(-z_j)), plus a weak term pushing the bottom 50% patches towards normal (weight 0.1, reflecting that most of an abnormal image is normal tissue). Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, PRO and image AUROC on the held-out modality; per-level localisation quality.
RATIONALE: A normal image carries a pixel-level label for free: every one of its patches is normal. Only abnormal images are ambiguous. MVFA's segmentation branch ignores this and needs masks for both. An asymmetric objective supervises all patches of normal images directly and only the most anomalous patches of abnormal images (multiple-instance), using the SigLIP many-to-one patch-text loss that MadCLIP brought to medical AD.
METHOD: 1) train_zero.py: replace the seg_loss block (Focal + Dice, only if seg_idx > 0) with asym_mil_loss(seg_patch_tokens, text_feature, image_label) applied to every image regardless of seg_idx. 2) New function in loss.py: asym_mil_loss computes per-level cosines (tokens L2-normalised as in MVFA), logits with learnable t (init 10) and b (init -5) (nn.Parameters added to the seg optimizer), normal images: all patches; abnormal images: top-k positive term + 0.1 x bottom-50% negative term; sum over the four levels. 3) The detection branch keeps its mean-pooled BCE. 4) Hyper-parameters: k = 6 (ablations 3, 12, 29), Adam lr 1e-4 as in the released zero-shot script, 50 epochs, batch size 1 as in the code (ablation: 16 with gradient accumulation, the paper's value). 5) Inference unchanged (test_zero.py).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); masks of the source datasets are discarded for all image-label-supervised variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities using image AUROC only (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds; evaluation on the held-out modalities that have masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) for pixel metrics and on all six for image AUROC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA (reference); symmetric top-k MIL; mean-pooled BCE on the seg branch (MVFA's detection loss applied to segmentation). Ablations: k; bottom-50% term on/off; SigLIP vs. softmax-CE patch loss; which levels receive the loss. Metrics: pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC, (AUROC-0.5) retention ratio. Falsification: retention below 60% or no gain over symmetric MIL.
